stem: Which manoeuvre in the paediatric motor examination most directly adds a turning challenge to gait assessment in a 4-year-old?
explanation: 180° manoeuvre is the correct answer because it directly challenges turning during gait assessment in a child who can already walk in a straight line.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because heel walking assesses balance and lower limb control but does not specifically test turning.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the 180° manoeuvre specifically adds a turning component to the gait examination.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because toe walking is a gait task, but it does not specifically focus on changing direction quickly.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the Romberg test assesses postural stability rather than turning during gait.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because prone assessment evaluates a different part of the motor examination and is not a gait manoeuvre.
